description: Backend Express prediction proxy routes. Adds backend/src/routes/predictions.ts (all routes JWT-protected via the existing `authenticate` middleware) that proxy to the ML service (FEAT-001) at process.env.ML_SERVICE_URL (default http://localhost:8000), and mounts them at /api/predictions in backend/src/index.ts. Uses the native global fetch (Node 20; @types/node provides the types) — NO axios is added (backend/package.json already has none). Build-toolchain: tsc; verification is `npx tsc --noEmit`. Runtime depends on FEAT-001 being up; the TS build is independent.
steps: Create backend/src/routes/predictions.ts. Pattern follows backend/src/routes/loads.ts and dashboard.ts. `const ML_SERVICE_URL = process.env.ML_SERVICE_URL || 'http://localhost:8000';`. `const router = Router();`. Use the global `fetch` (no import). All routes use the `authenticate` middleware (import from '../middleware/auth'). Routes: GET /rate -> read req.query {market, equipmentType, distance, dayOfWeek, fuelPrice}; POST JSON {market, equipment_type: equipmentType, distance: Number(distance), day_of_week: Number(dayOfWeek), fuel_price: Number(fuelPrice)} to `${ML_SERVICE_URL}/predict/rate`; return upstream JSON. GET /fuel/:market -> proxy GET `${ML_SERVICE_URL}/fuel/price/:market`. GET /fuel-cost -> read req.query {market, distance}; POST JSON {market, distance: Number(distance)} to `${ML_SERVICE_URL}/fuel/cost`; return upstream JSON. GET /demand/:market -> proxy GET `${ML_SERVICE_URL}/demand/heatmap/:market`. POST /demand/forecast -> forward req.body to `${ML_SERVICE_URL}/demand/forecast`; return upstream JSON. Error handling: helper that, given a fetch result, if !res.ok reads the upstream body (await res.json()) and returns res.status(upstream.status).json(body); if fetch throws, return res.status(502).json({error: 'ML service unavailable'}). Wrap each handler in async (req,res) => try/catch. IMPORTANT route order: put /rate, /fuel-cost before /fuel/:market and /demand/:market so the static paths are not swallowed by the :market params (mirror the loads.ts comment about named routes before /:id).

Modify backend/src/index.ts: add `import predictionsRoutes from './routes/predictions';` with the other route imports, and add `app.use('/api/predictions', predictionsRoutes);` next to the existing app.use('/api/loads', ...) mount. Do not change anything else.
Modify backend/.env.example: append `ML_SERVICE_URL=http://localhost:8000` after the existing FRONTEND_URL line.
Do NOT add axios. Confirm backend/package.json is unchanged (axios must not be a dependency).
acceptance_criteria: backend/src/index.ts contains `app.use('/api/predictions', predictionsRoutes);` and the matching import.
backend/src/routes/predictions.ts imports `authenticate` from '../middleware/auth' and applies it to every route.
No axios dependency added to backend/package.json.
verification: Run `cd backend && npx tsc --noEmit` and confirm exit code 0 (0 errors).
Run `grep -n "api/predictions" backend/src/index.ts` and confirm the mount line and import are present.
Run `grep -n "authenticate" backend/src/routes/predictions.ts` and confirm every route handler is protected.
Run `grep -c 'axios' backend/package.json` and confirm it is unchanged (axios was already absent -> 0).
findings: Implemented backend/src/routes/predictions.ts with all 5 routes (GET /rate, GET /fuel-cost, POST /demand/forecast, GET /fuel/:market, GET /demand/:market) behind the existing `authenticate` middleware. Uses the native global `fetch` (Node 20 / @types/node) — no axios added. Static routes (/rate, /fuel-cost, POST /demand/forecast) registered before /:market params so they are not swallowed. Upstream non-2xx forwarded with status+body; network failures return 502 {error}. Mounted at /api/predictions in index.ts; ML_SERVICE_URL appended to .env.example. Verified: `npx tsc --noEmit` -> 0 errors; grep shows mount+import; every route protected by `authenticate`; axios count in backend/package.json = 0.
